newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota stock index ends up 6 pct at two-year high.
newsitem.headline: Bogota stock index ends up 6 pct at two-year high.

text.p: The Bogota stock exchange IBB index ended Monday's session up 6.03 percent at 1,004.27, its highest level since Jan. 18, 1995, brokers said.

The rise was fueled by demand from foreign funds, local insurance companies and pensions funds for bluechips, particularly banks and the leading companies of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate.
Brokers reported a total volume of 3.17 billion pesos on the Bogota exchange.
The heaviest demand was for cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, insurance company Suramericana, Bancoquia bank, the Banco Industrial Colombiano and brewing giant Bavaria.

Brokers said there were several factors at work driving up Colombian stocks. They said Colombian shares, which have seen little price variation in the last three years are considered very cheap coupled with relatively expensive prices on Wall Street.
New regulations, introduced on Jan. 1, mean fixed income investors have been saddled with a new tax of between 1 percent and 7 percent on earnings depending on the maturity of the paper.
In addition, changes in the way Colombian pension funds are obliged to calculate annual returns have also stimulated demand for stocks, brokers said.
